chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Rooming houses, buses and no hotels for black musicians in the South
summary: They discuss rooming houses full of bedbugs, travelling by bus and hotels that would not take black guests; he says the early 1930s were bad.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In a way I guess it was better when you were on the road in those days to go to places like a rooming house or -- which was sort of place where they catered to musicians -- than going to a hotel like they do now. And going to a hotel and it's probably more expensive even by --
Oh it is -- it is expensive.
Those rooming houses weren't too hot
either. A lot of places had a lot of bedbugs and things. Oh yes, you know, and that's no fun. Yeah. I think hotels would have been better because all the guys would have been together.
At rooming houses and things like that, guys were scattered all over -- you know. There were sections --
Were most of you driving your own cars then, or was it that you rode the bus.
Well then it would a -- maybe a problem sometimes getting everybody to the job on time and getting everybody to the place on time --

Yeah, yeah. It was kind of rough that way, yeah. Wherein if you just stayed at a hotel -- but there was no hotels -- the hotels wouldn't take no colored in that town at that time you know. That'd be way before KIng.
You know. Way back in '40 -- times was rough.
Was it worse in the '40s than it had been a little earlier -- in the '20s and --
Well, I don't know about the '20s -- I know the early '30s was pretty bad down there. I -- I mean lots of times -- next time we come and get together I'll tell you about it.
